input:
Two sides of a triangle are sqrt(3) + 1 and sqrt(3) - 1 and the included angle is 60 degrees, then the difference of the remaining angles is

Options:
A. 30 degrees
B. 45 degrees
C. 60 degrees
D. 90 degrees

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Given two sides and included angle, determine the difference between the other two angles.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Find third side by cosine rule, then one remaining angle by sine rule.

key_formulas.sine_rule: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Compute c, then obtain one angle and use sum to get the other, finally take difference.
logical_steps: Step 1: Use cosine rule to find c
Step 2: Use sine rule to find B
Step 3: Compute A from angle sum

step_2_find_angle_B.sine_rule_form: sin B / b = sin C / c

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: Computed remaining angles are 105 degrees and 15 degrees, so their difference is 90 degrees.
